pipeline_name: Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System

validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE and CLASSIFICATION confirmed independently of GEM/gem.wiki (this row has no wiki page -- 'wiki' is blank in the worklist). This is Great Basin Gas Transmission Company's '2028 Expansion Project,' a proposed interstate natural gas transmission expansion in six Nevada counties (Churchill, Humboldt, Lyon, Pershing, Storey, Washoe) on Great Basin's existing 898-mile system (formerly Paiute Pipeline, wholly owned subsidiary of Southwest Gas Corporation). Confirmed via: (1) Southwest Gas Holdings' own SEC 8-K press release (filed 2026-06-05... actually dated June 2025) announcing the Binding Open Season results for the '2028 Expansion Project'; (2) FERC's Federal Register Notice of Intent to prepare an EA / scoping notice (FR Doc 2026-08459, published 2026-04-30), confirming FERC opened a PRE-FILING docket, No. PF26-5-000, on 2026-01-20, for 'Great Basin's 2028 Expansion Project,' describing planned construction of ~195 mi of new 42-inch pipeline + ~15 mi of new 24-inch lateral pipeline, a new Jungo Road Compressor Station (Humboldt County), a new receipt point adjacent to the existing Opal Valley Receipt Point, and abandonment of ~142 mi of existing 1960s-era 8-/16-inch pipe plus the existing Rye Patch and Lovelock Compressor Stations; (3) Great Basin's own current project microsite (expansion2028.greatbasingtcprojects.com) and its dated August 2026 Fact Sheet PDF, which frames the project as in 'Planning & Development Phase,' anticipated in-service November 2028, with 'Submit FERC application' still a pending 2026 milestone (i.e. no formal NGA section 7 certificate application has been filed as of this sweep -- only the pre-filing docket). CLASSIFICATION confirmed: interstate natural gas transmission pipeline expansion, correctly classified as gas/transmission/proposed. As of this sweep (2026-09-15) no FERC certificate order has issued and no construction has begun -- 'proposed' remains correct (see status_reviews).

validity.researcher_notes: Confirmed P7860 is NOT a duplicate/relabeling of any sibling in the 'Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System' cluster (P7856-P7860), and specifically not of P7859 despite an EIA data-quality wrinkle (below). Distinguishing facts: P7856 = the 898-mi Main Line itself (operating). P7857 = '2024 Expansion Project,' FERC Docket CP23-466-000, filed 2023-05-01, 3.41 mi (0.25 mi 20-in loop + 2.88 mi 10-in->20-in replacement + 0.28 mi 12-in loop), 5,674 Dth/d incremental capacity. P7858 = 'Gabbs Lateral Naval Air Station Fallon (NASF) Relocation Project,' FERC Docket CP25-551-000 (pre-filing PF24-6-000), filed 2025-09-29. P7859 = '2026 Expansion Project,' FERC Docket CP25-209-000, filed 2025-04-15, 2.32-4.67 mi loop/replacement, 8,129 Dth/d incremental capacity. P7860 (this row) = '2028 Expansion Project,' FERC PRE-FILING Docket PF26-5-000 (opened 2026-01-20; no CP-docket certificate application filed yet as of 2026-08 per the company's own project timeline), a materially larger project spanning six counties, ~195 mi of new 42-in pipe + ~15 mi of new 24-in lateral pipe (~210 mi total new construction) plus abandonment of ~142 mi of old 8-/16-in pipe, targeting ~800 MMcf/d (per EIA's most current releases, based on binding precedent agreements) to as much as 948,000 Dth/d (per the company's own August 2026 Fact Sheet) of incremental capacity, in-service targeted November 2028, capital cost ~$1.7B (EIA) vs. an earlier June-2025 Southwest Gas estimate of $800M-$1.2B. EIA DATA-QUALITY NOTE (relevant to the misattribution precedent the orchestrator flagged): EIA's own 'Great Basin Expansion Project' row (Natural Gas Pipeline Projects sheet, present in the 2026-01/05/08 releases) is confirmed to be THIS row (P7860, the 2028 Expansion) by its own Notes text -- 'Larger 2028 Expansion in pre-filing discussions with FERC,' explicitly distinguished in the same Notes from 'a smaller 2026 Expansion (~8,129 Dth/d)... filed FERC CP25-209-000 on 4/15/2025' (i.e. P7859) -- but the Aug-2026 release's 'Docket/Permit Number' FIELD (as opposed to the Notes prose) is populated with 'CP25-209-000,' which is actually P7859's docket, not P7860's. This is an EIA data-entry error in that one structured field, not evidence the two rows are the same project -- the correct docket citation for P7860 is FERC PF26-5-000 / Federal Register FR Doc 2026-08459, never any EIA-stated 'CP25-209-000.' Routed as informational here; no cross_row_lead needed since P7859's own shard already resolved this correctly.

validity.recommendation: Correct LengthKnown from 0.00 to ~210 mi (195 mi new 42-in mainline loop + 15 mi new 24-in lateral, per FERC's own scoping notice) and Diameter from blank to 42,24 in. The sheet's 0.00/blank pairing is currently cited to the pgjonline.com article, but that article never states a segment mileage at all -- it only mentions Great Basin's existing 898-mile SYSTEM total, which is a different scope (aggregate-vs-segment rule) -- so the Length cell was effectively uncited despite carrying a [ref]. Two independent, current, primary sources (FERC's own regulatory scoping notice and Great Basin's own August-2026 Fact Sheet) agree the 2028 Expansion Project involves substantial NEW physical pipe, not zero -- but they disagree on the exact total: FERC's itemized figure sums to 210 mi (195+15); the company's own Fact Sheet instead states 'approximately 230 miles of natural gas pipeline and associated facilities' (no diameter breakdown given). That is a genuine, unreconciled ~9.5% delta between two credible primary sources (regulator vs. applicant), not simple rounding -- recommend using FERC's itemized 195+15=210 mi / 42,24-in figures (more granular, matches the Diameter field's need for a breakdown) as the staged fill, with the company's differing 230-mi aggregate flagged here for reconciliation once a formal certificate application (with a final engineering route sheet) is filed.
validity.researcher_notes: Checked the pgjonline.com article word-for-word: it states only 'the company's 898-mile transmission system' (the Main Line total, P7856's scope) and gives no segment-specific mileage or diameter for the 2028 Expansion -- confirms the current [ref] does not actually support LengthKnown=0.00/Diameter=blank. FERC's Notice of Intent To Prepare an Environmental Assessment / scoping notice (FR Doc 2026-08459, published 2026-04-30, Docket PF26-5-000): 'The 2028 Expansion Project would consist of approximately 195 miles of new 42-inch-diameter pipeline and approximately 15 miles of new 24-inch-diameter lateral pipelines... [and] the planned abandonment of approximately 142 miles of existing, mostly 1960s-era, 8- and 16-inch-diameter pipeline and the existing Rye Patch and Lovelock Compressor Stations.' Great Basin's own August 2026 Fact Sheet (expansion2028.greatbasingtcprojects.com): 'Installation of approximately 230 miles of natural gas pipeline and associated facilities, one new compressor station, and modifications to existing infrastructure' -- confirms substantial new construction and the abandonment total (~142 mi, matching FERC) but gives a higher aggregate new-mileage figure with no diameter split. Both sources independently rule out 0.00/blank as correct; staged the FERC figure as the primary fill (see fills[]) and filed this as a spec concern rather than silently picking one number, since a formal certificate application (which would carry the definitive engineering figure) has not yet been filed.

validity.recommendation: Capacity=1250.00 MMcf/d is sourced (the cited pgjonline.com article does state 'approximately 1.25 billion cubic feet per day,' via unit equivalence 1.25 Bcf/d = 1250 MMcf/d -- kept as REVERIFIED, see fills[]) but it is Southwest Gas's own June-2025 PRE-close estimate, based on 'indicative capacity requests' before the Binding Open Season and its two supplemental rounds had even closed. Two later, more current sources give materially different figures and disagree with EACH OTHER: EIA's own May/Aug-2026 releases state 'nearly 800 MMcf/d of binding precedent agreements' actually secured across three completed open seasons (closing 5/28/2025, 11/11/2025, and December 2025) -- EIA's Jan-2026 release had shown 1,760 MMcf/d, since revised down; while Great Basin's own August-2026 Fact Sheet instead states the project 'adds up to approximately 948,000 dekatherms per day' (~948 MMcf/d, roughly Dth/Mcf-equivalent) of new capacity -- a THIRD figure, using 'up to,' suggesting a maximum/design capacity rather than the contracted 800 MMcf/d EIA reports. Recommend investigating and updating once the formal FERC application publishes a definitive contracted capacity figure; in the meantime EIA's 800 MMcf/d (grounded in EIA's own description of actual signed binding precedent agreements, the most concrete and recent commercial fact available) is the better-evidenced replacement candidate over the stale 1250, but the company's own newer 948,000 Dth/d figure is a live, unreconciled alternative -- not confident enough in either single number to overwrite Capacity outright, so left the candidate value blank here pending that reconciliation.
validity.researcher_notes: pgj/SEC (June 2025, 8-K press release, single origin): 'Approximately 1.25 billion cubic feet per day of incremental transportation capacity' -- an ESTIMATE based on indicative (non-binding) capacity requests, explicitly framed as subject to change pending final negotiated precedent agreements. EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, 'Great Basin Expansion Project' row: Jan-2026 release = 1,760 MMcf/d; May-2026 and Aug-2026 releases both = 800 MMcf/d, with EIA's own Notes text explaining the drop: 'Binding open season closed 5/28/2025, followed by supplemental open seasons (one closing 11/11/2025, a second closing December 2025) that together secured nearly 800 MMcf/d of binding precedent agreements (20-year minimum term)' -- i.e. EIA's revision reflects the ACTUAL contracted outcome of the open season process the pgj estimate predated. Great Basin's own August-2026 Fact Sheet: 'Adds up to approximately 948,000 dekatherms per day of new natural gas transportation capacity' -- current as of the same month as this sweep, from the applicant itself, but does not reconcile with EIA's 800 MMcf/d figure and uses 'up to' phrasing. All three figures trace to genuinely different vintages/definitions (indicative estimate vs. contracted binding capacity vs. a design/maximum figure), not a simple correction chain -- filed as a material, unresolved spec concern per rule 5 rather than silently staging any one of them as a correction.

Full timeline reconstructed: Southwest Gas's Binding Open Season Notice posted 2025-01-28 -> Open Season closed 2025-06-05 (with two supplemental rounds through Dec 2025) -> Great Basin requested FERC pre-filing review, granted as Docket PF26-5-000 opened 2026-01-20 -> FERC's Notice of Intent/scoping notice published 2026-04-30 (comment deadline 2026-05-21) -> as of the company's own Aug-2026 Fact Sheet, 'Submit FERC application' is still a pending, not-yet-completed, 2026 milestone. Two distinct, current origins (the company's own site + FERC) agree. No sale, withdrawal, or suspension found anywhere.

summary: P7860 = Great Basin Gas Transmission Company's '2028 Expansion Project' -- FERC pre-filing Docket PF26-5-000 (opened 2026-01-20; no CP certificate application filed yet) -- confirmed real, correctly classified, and NOT a duplicate of P7856-P7859 (each a distinct FERC docket/scope on the same system); distinguished by its own docket, its 6-county footprint (Churchill/Humboldt/Lyon/Pershing/Storey/Washoe), and its materially larger scope (~210 mi new 42/24-in pipe vs. each sibling's smaller mileage). All 15 worklist units carry records: 10 sourced (REVERIFIED: Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity; REFS_ADDED: Proposal/Start/Length/Diameter/SegmentCost/Location/Operator/Owner) and 4 UNRESOLVED (Construction/Pressure/FuelSource -- nothing found, consistent with the project's pre-filing stage). Two material spec concerns filed: (1) LengthKnown/Diameter (0.00/blank is uncited -- FERC states ~210 mi new 42/24-in pipe, but the company's own Fact Sheet gives a differing ~230 mi total); (2) Capacity (1250 MMcf/d is a stale June-2025 estimate, superseded by two later, mutually-disagreeing figures: EIA's 800 MMcf/d of contracted binding agreements vs. the company's own 'up to' 948,000 Dth/d).
